text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- A rapid pick-up in construction may lead to a lack of building materials in the summer, particularly windows, kitchen furniture and roofing felt, industry lobby says.
- Helsinki electricity grid operator Helsingin Energia beats other large Finnish companies in comparison of profits to turnover and profits per employee.
- Parliament now through first half of its term, and the most important issue for the other half is Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
- Finance ministry has appointed too many men and too few women to its committees with only one of seven committees meeting the gender quota criterion.

- Technical obstacles capped telephone tapping last year and police listened to only five telephones in investigating three crimes, ministry of interior says in report to parliament's justice obudsman.
- Security chief at Estonian Georg Ots passenger ferry was caught trying to smuggle one kg of amphetamine into Finland, Finnish authorities say.
- Top-speed digital ATM (Asynchronous Transfer Mode) networks spreading in Finland and expected to be commonly used by corporations and public organisations in a couple of years.

- Personnel funds improve capitalism which is in crisis and where faceless ownership means that employees do not know who is responsible for them, says Aatos Erkko, main owner and chairman of the board of media house Sanoma Osakeyhtio.
- Swiss army buying bullet-proof vests for 35 million markka from Finnish KE-Burgmann, corresponding to one year's net sales for the company.
KAUPPALEHTI
- An agreed five percent rise in logwood prices will become expensive for independent sawmills which will have weak profits this year after two years' losses, sawmill lobby says.
- Pepsi-Cola to market Finnish Valio's juices and spring water in Russia and the cooperation may double Valio's sales there to 7-8 million litres this year.
- Power and machinery firm Kyro Oy plans share issue and listing to finance investments and acquisitions, CEO Pentti Yliheljo says.

- U.S. software company Geoworks shares -- of which Nokia owns 7.3 percent -- have plunged almost 40 percent on the Nasdaq list on the company's profit warning last week. The company designs software for Nokia's 9000 Communicator which combines a palmtop computer with a digital mobile phone.

- UPM-Kymmene source says the company is likely to bid for indebted Canadian light-weight-coated paper maker Repap which has modern machines and a leading market position, should shareholders of Repap and Avenor reject a merger plan on Wednesday.
AAMULEHTI
- Finland has requested the European Commission to ban the use of two kinds of fodder anti-biotics by next year.
DEMARI

- Parliament's constitutional committee should give a statement on how parliament should decide on Finnish membership of European economic and monetary union (EMU), says Erkki Tuomioja, chairman of the Social Democratic Party parliamentary group.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET

- Hornet jet fighters bought by the Finnish air force are sensitive to dust and gravel, and tarmacs have to be swept before landing and take off, but the problem is common to all jet planes, airforce officer says.
